A free hull is drawn at schedule + Fleet::DrawnOffsetOf (evasion + sim separation + drawnSeparation, km, placed via KmToSceneNear in UnitySpaceApp::UpdateShips, Main2.cpp ~1184); a piloted one at PilotedScene() (Cruise.cpp 595) with no drawn offset, and EnterPiloting (UnitySpaceApp.cpp 994) seeds the pilot from ShipHelm::FrameOf -> Fleet::StateOf (schedule + EvasionOf only, no drawnSeparation). So at game scale on a take the fighter jumps by its drawn sidestep (~22 units in the T477 CSV, frame 396: fighter at (8882,663,16474) drawn, (8900,657,16484) true), and the battleship's drawn solve changes because the fighter becomes a held weight-0 body at its undisplaced spot and gains the DrawnViewHull camera-line Axis/Reach term (Fleet.cpp 409-422, switched on by IsPiloting in UpdateShips ~1036) -> +17.7 then -26. On let-go (ExitPiloting, UnitySpaceApp.cpp 1149, PinWherePiloted) the fighter becomes Separable again and the drawn solve at once pushes it off the nearby battleship (8.4 and 2.1 units, frame 3109). Fix idea: ease the view's drawn offsets across a hand-off instead of snapping them, e.g. Fleet keeps a per-hull eased drawnSeparation (time-constant ~0.5 s, also applied to the held hull, drawn at PilotedScene + its eased offset, and the held body in the drawn solve placed at that drawn spot), and/or fade the DrawnViewAxis Reach in over the fly-in; alternative for the take only: seed the pilot at schedule + DrawnOffsetOf (moves the true pose by the game-scale sidestep, a few km). Request(design, catalogue, callback): game thread gathers ImportedGeometry::Of per asset (extend ImportedGeometry with Normals from StaticMeshVertexBuffer.VertexTangentZ and Uv0 from GetVertexUV, guarded by GetTangentData/GetTexCoordData non-null); Async(EAsyncExecution::ThreadPool) builds one FMeshDescription (FStaticMeshAttributes, one polygon group per material key = atlas or starsparrow or box): part vertex = design pose * scale(mirrored ? -s : s, s, s) * (middle-or-0 + fit.Turn * v * fit.Scale), back to Unreal cm as (ux, -uz, uy) * 100; keep imported triangle order (already Unreal winding) but swap b,c for mirrored parts and for Unity-wound box parts (MeshFactory::BuiltinCube; see UnityScene.cpp Builder::Tri). Then AsyncTask(GameThread): NewObject<UStaticMesh>(GetTransientPackage(), SG_Design_<hash>, RF_Transient), AddToRoot, one FStaticMaterial per section, BuildFromMeshDescriptions with bMarkPackageDirty=false; bFastBuild=true normally; when any part is Nanite and WITH_EDITOR, GetNaniteSettings().bEnabled=true, bCommitMeshDescription=true, bFastBuild=false (note: Build(true) inside is synchronous on the game thread, so consider UStaticMesh::Build async compile or accept a one-off cost). Wrap as cs::Ref<Mesh> with ImportedAsset = sm->GetPathName(), ImportedScale = 0.01, bounds from the design box, cached by hash; materials per section via MaterialOf. Instancing: every ship shares the one Mesh (one UStaticMesh); and in UnityScene.cpp InstancedBatch::Flush use LoadObject of mesh->ImportedAsset instead of StaticMeshOf when set, premultiplying each transform by ImportedCorrection(mesh->ImportedScale, mesh->ImportedRotation) as the renderer does (UnityScene.cpp ~798). Wire sg.Assemble: show the per-part model at once, swap to one MeshRenderer with the merged mesh (SetSharedMaterials) when the callback fires, keep EnginePorts marks.
